page: Microsoft Azure F8ads_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing a direct mapping of vCPUs to physical cores without hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The hypervisor layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

In benchmark evaluations, the F8ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET operations, also perform at average levels. For machine learning workloads, text generation using a small 135M model achieves top-tier speeds, while prompt processing and larger model inference remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F8ads_v7 offers high single-core compute density and dedicated physical resources, which reduces virtualization overhead. The inclusion of a 945 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage without requiring separate storage attachments, though the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio may limit memory-bound workloads. The lack of hyperthreading means users get full physical cores, which benefits compute-bound tasks but limits the total concurrent thread count compared to hyperthreaded alternatives.

This server configuration is suited for workloads requiring strong single-threaded performance and fast local storage. Appropriate use cases include relational databases, web serving, single-threaded data processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.
